sources.news_title: Hit in the Iranian Sky: u.s. Fighter Shot Down, Rescues One of His Crew
sources.text:
Washington-3 de abril de 2026-Total News Agency-TNA- La guerra en Oriente Medio dio este viernes un salto tan delicado como simbólico: un avión de combate de Estados Unidos cayó en territorio de Irán y, en medio de una operación de altísimo riesgo, fuerzas norteamericanas lograron rescatar con vida a uno de los dos tripulantes. El episodio, confirmado por medios estadounidenses y respaldado por fuentes citadas por Reuters, The Washington Post y CBS News, marcó el primer caso conocido de una aeronave militar tripulada de Estados Unidos abatida o perdida dentro de territorio iraní desde que comenzó esta nueva fase del conflicto regional. El dato sacudió a Washington, expuso que el régimen iraní todavía conserva capacidad de respuesta sobre su espacio aéreo y volvió a demostrar que, pese a los mensajes triunfalistas de la administración de Donald Trump, la guerra está lejos de estar bajo control total.
De acuerdo con la información que circuló durante la jornada, la aeronave sería un F-15E Strike Eagle de la Fuerza Aérea de Estados Unidos, un caza biplaza utilizado en misiones de ataque profundo. Dos fuentes estadounidenses dijeron a Reuters que se trató de un aparato de dos asientos y que, tras el incidente, se activó de inmediato una misión de búsqueda. Poco después, medios israelíes y estadounidenses informaron que uno de los tripulantes había sido recuperado con vida, mientras continuaba el operativo para hallar al segundo. The Washington Post agregó que el rescate se desarrolló en el sur de Irán y que la condición del militar evacuado no había sido detallada oficialmente, aunque se sabía que estaba recibiendo atención médica.
El otro tripulante, en cambio, seguía siendo una incógnita al cierre de esta jornada. Esa incertidumbre volvió todavía más dramática una misión que, según especialistas citados por The Washington Post, figura entre las más peligrosas que puede ejecutar el aparato militar estadounidense: ingresar en territorio hostil, con helicópteros y aeronaves volando bajo, para recuperar personal aislado antes de que sea capturado o eliminado por fuerzas enemigas. El diario reportó incluso imágenes verificadas de un C-130 reabasteciendo en vuelo a helicópteros HH-60G dentro de Irán, una postal que pinta por sí sola el nivel de riesgo asumido por Washington para evitar que uno de sus hombres quedara en manos del régimen.
Sobre la causa de la caída todavía no hubo una explicación oficial cerrada. Ahí está una de las claves del episodio. Reuters informó que un funcionario estadounidense confirmó que la aeronave fue derribada, mientras que la Guardia Revolucionaria iraní sostuvo que su defensa antiaérea la alcanzó en el sudoeste del país. Sin embargo, The Washington Post advirtió que también persistían dudas sobre si pudo haber existido una falla mecánica o un accidente combinado con fuego enemigo. En paralelo, medios estatales iraníes lanzaron otra versión exagerada y hablaron de un F-35, algo que no fue confirmado por fuentes estadounidenses y que varios reportes independientes pusieron en duda. Más allá de esas disputas narrativas, el hecho central no cambió: una aeronave de combate de Estados Unidos terminó en tierra dentro de Irán, y eso ya constituye un revés militar y político muy difícil de maquillar.
El episodio adquiere todavía más peso porque llega en un momento en que Trump y el secretario de Defensa Pete Hegseth venían insistiendo en que las fuerzas norteamericanas dominaban por completo los cielos iraníes. Esa idea quedó seriamente golpeada. The Washington Post recordó que el presidente había dicho apenas días antes que Irán ya no tenía defensa antiaérea efectiva y que las fuerzas estadounidenses eran “imparables”. La caída del F-15E contradice de frente esa narrativa y abre una nueva discusión dentro de Estados Unidos sobre el verdadero costo de la operación Furia Épica, el nombre con el que la Casa Blanca bautizó su campaña contra Teherán. El mismo medio señaló que, hasta ahora, trece militares estadounidenses murieron y centenares resultaron heridos desde el inicio de la guerra.
También hay un dato que agrava todavía más el cuadro: este sería el cuarto F-15 perdido desde que comenzó la campaña militar, aunque los tres casos anteriores ocurrieron en Kuwait por fuego amigo y con rescate exitoso de todos los tripulantes. Esta vez fue distinto. Esta vez el golpe fue en pleno territorio enemigo, con un tripulante ya rescatado, otro todavía desaparecido y con el régimen iraní tratando de convertir la escena en propaganda. En un conflicto que ya venía escalando por el cierre de Ormuz, los ataques sobre infraestructura y la presión sobre aliados regionales, la caída del avión introdujo un elemento nuevo y peligroso: la posibilidad de que la guerra empiece a mostrar con más frecuencia pérdidas directas y visibles para Estados Unidos, algo que en Washington siempre termina pesando tanto en el frente militar como en el político.

sources.news_title: Iran Downed a Us Fighter Jet
sources.text:
Iran pudotti Yhdysvaltojen hävittäjän
Iranin armeija pudotti perjantaina yhdysvaltalaisen hävittäjän Iranissa. Iranilaisen uutistoimisto Farsin mukaan Iranin ilmatorjunta ampui koneen alas maan keskiosassa.
Yhdysvallat vahvisti koneen alasampumisen. Yhdysvaltalaismedian mukaan koneen miehistön toinen jäsen oli pelastettu ja toimitettu hoitoon. Toisen etsinnät olivat käynnissä perjantai-iltana Suomen aikaa.
Myös Iran etsi toista miehistön jäsentä ja kertoi maksavansa palkkion koneen pilotin tai pilottien toimittamisesta viranomaisille elossa.
Yhdysvaltalaisten medioiden mukaan alas ammuttu kone oli F-15E-hävittäjä. Iranilaismediat julkaisivat kuvia, jotka niiden mukaan näyttivät alas ammutun yhdysvaltalaisen hävittäjän jäänteitä.
Iranilaismedioissa väitettiin jäänteiden olleen F-35-hävittäjästä, mutta yhdysvaltalaisten medioiden haastattelemien asiantuntijoiden mukaan ne näyttivät olevan F-15-hävittäjästä.
Iran ei ollut aiemmin tämän sodan aikana onnistunut ampumaan alas Yhdysvaltojen hävittäjää. Tosin sodan alussa Kuwaitin ilmatorjunta ampui vahingossa alas kolme Yhdysvaltojen F-15-hävittäjää.
Samoihin aikoihin myös toinen yhdysvaltalaiskone putosi Persianlahden alueella, kertoi New York Times, jonka lähteiden mukaan koneen pilotti saatiin pelastettua. Lehden mukaan A-10 Warthog -maataistelukone putosi lähellä Hormuzinsalmea.
Iranin armeija kertoo myöhemmin pudottaneensa koneen Persianlahteen, maan valtiollinen televisio kertoi.
Iran yhä iskukykyinen
Yhdysvaltalaistiedustelu arvioi, että Iranilla on yhä käytössään noin puolet ohjuslaukaisimistaan ja drooneistaan. Asiasta kertoi uutiskanava CNN tiedustelutietoja tuntevien lähteidensä pohjalta.
Arvion perusteella osa ohjuslaukaisimista on voinut hautautua maan alle Yhdysvaltojen ja Israelin Iraniin tekemien iskujen vuoksi, mutta laukaisimet eivät ole tuhoutuneet.
Tiedustelutietojen perusteella Iranilla on ohjuslaukaisimiensa lisäksi suuri määrä ohjuksia. Lähteiden mukaan Iranilla on yhä myös tuhansia drooneja.
Tiedustelutiedot on CNN:n mukaan koottu viime päivinä. Tiedoista selviää myös, että suuri osa Iranin rannikkopuolustuksen risteilyohjuksista on yhä käyttökelpoisia. Kyseiset ohjukset ovat avainasemassa, kun Iran pitää öljynkuljetuksille tärkeää Hormuzinsalmea hallinnassaan.
Yhdysvaltain asevoimien mukaan maa oli iskenyt keskiviikkoon mennessä yli 12 300 kohteeseen Iranin sisällä. CNN:n lähteiden mukaan tiedustelutiedot osoittavat, että Yhdysvaltain asevoimat on heikentänyt Iranin sotilaallisia kykyjä.
Iranista ohjuksia Israelia kohti
Tiedusteluarviot eroavat huomattavasti presidentti Donald Trumpin puheista. Yhdysvaltain aikaa keskiviikkona Trump piti yhdysvaltalaisille puheen, jossa hän muun muassa sanoi, että Iranin ohjuskapasiteetti on lähestulkoon käytetty tai tuhottu.
Trumpin lausuntojen uskottavuutta nakersi jokseenkin sekin, että pian puheen jälkeen Yhdysvaltain läheinen liittolainen Israel ilmoitti ohjusaalloista, joita Iranista oli laukaistu Israelia kohti.
Perjantain vastaisena yönä Israelin asevoimat kertoi jälleen, että Iranista oli laukaistu ohjuksia Israelia kohti.

sources.news_title: Iran Hunts Second US Crew Member After F-15E Shot Down, One Rescued
sources.text:
A United States Air Force F-15E Strike Eagle fighter jet has been shot down over Iran, with one of its two crew members rescued alive by American special forces and a search underway for the second, US officials and multiple major news organisations confirmed on Friday, April 3, 2026.
One of two crew members of the downed US fighter jet was located and rescued by US special forces, with the search for the second still ongoing, according to an Israeli official and a second source with knowledge of the situation.
One of the US sources confirmed the aircraft was an F-15E Strike Eagle, a Boeing-made jet capable of carrying out both air-to-air and air-to-ground missions. F-15Es typically fly with a two-member crew: a pilot and a weapons systems officer. The rescued crew member is alive and receiving medical attention.
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed responsibility for the shootdown. Iranian state media released photographs of what it claimed was the wreckage of the aircraft, showing a partial logo for “US Air Forces in Europe” on a tail fin and red-and-white striping consistent with an F-15. A second piece of wreckage bore text that aviation analysts said matched the rear portion of an F-15 between one of its two engines and its horizontal stabiliser.
Iran’s Tasnim news agency said the search for the missing crew member had “so far been unsuccessful,” while Fars News reported that a reward was being offered for anyone who finds the crew alive. Local traders in Kohgiluyeh and Boyer-Ahmad Province offered 10 billion tomans, equivalent to approximately $76,000, for anyone who locates the crew.
Israel cancelled planned strikes in Iran to avoid hampering the search and rescue effort, and is assisting the United States with intelligence to locate the second crew member.
This marks the first time a manned US aircraft has been downed by enemy fire since the start of the military campaign, coming after repeated assertions by President Donald Trump, Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, and senior military commanders that Iran had been largely deprived of effective air defences. Trump was briefed on the incident, White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt confirmed.
The US has lost at least 16 MQ-9 Reaper drones over Iran since the war began. Three F-15 fighter jets were also previously shot down over Kuwait in a friendly fire incident early in the conflict, with no casualties in that instance.
The incident is developing rapidly. NewsGhana will provide updates as the situation evolves.

sources.news_title: Crew member rescued after US aircraft went down in Iran
sources.text:
Crew member rescued after US aircraft went down in Iran
One crew member has been rescued after an American aircraft went down in Iran, according to one U.S. and one Israeli official, who both spoke on condition of anonymity to describe sensitive ongoing military operations.
The rescue occurred as the U.S. military was conducting a search and rescue operation, according to three people familiar who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss the sensitivity of the situation. Israel is helping the United States with the search and rescue operation.
White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said in a statement that President Donald Trump had been briefed but did not offer any additional information.
It was the first time the U.S. has lost aircraft in Iranian territory and constitutes a dramatic escalation in the war since it began five weeks ago. It was not clear if the jet was shot down or crashed.
Iran fired on targets across the Mideast on Friday, as Tehran kept the pressure on Israel and its Gulf Arab neighbors, despite U.S. and Israeli insistence that Iran’s military capabilities have been all but destroyed.
Iran’s attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure and its tight grip on the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of the world’s oil and natural gas transits in peacetime, have roiled stock markets, sent oil prices skyrocketing, and threatened to raise the cost of many basic goods, including food.
Television anchor urges residents to hand over pilot
An anchor on a channel affiliated with Iranian state television urged residents to hand over any “enemy pilot” to police and promised a reward for anyone who did. The channel is in Kohkilouyeh and Boyer-Ahmad province, an intensely rural and mountainous region that spans over 15,500 square kilometers (5,900 square miles).
Authorities also urged the public to search for the pilot in neighboring Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari province.
Throughout the war, Iran has made a series of claims about shooting down piloted enemy aircraft that turned out not to be true. Friday was the first time that Iran went on television urging the public to look for a suspected downed pilot.
An on-screen crawl earlier urged the public to “shoot them if you see them,” referring to social media footage circulating of what appeared to be U.S. aircraft in the area. The channel showed metal debris in the back of a pickup truck while making the announcement but provided no other immediate details.

sources.text:
EE UU rescata a uno de los dos tripulantes del primer F-15E abatido en Irán, según CBS y fuentes israelíes
Irán
Teherán ofrece una "generosa recompensa" a quienes capturen a los pilotos
Madrid/Irán derribó este viernes un avión de combate de Estados Unidos en su territorio, según informaron funcionarios estadounidenses y medios próximos a Teherán. Se trata de un F-15E Strike Eagle de la Fuerza Aérea. Aunque por ahora se desconoce el lugar exacto donde ocurrió el incidente, The Washington Post lo sitúa en el suroeste de Irán.
Las autoridades estadounidenses activaron una operación de búsqueda y rescate para localizar a los dos tripulantes (piloto y oficial de armamento) que viajaban a bordo del caza. Esta sería la primera vez que Irán derriba un avión de combate estadounidense en su propio territorio desde el comienzo de la actual guerra en Oriente Medio.
La televisión estatal iraní instó además a la población a entregar a las autoridades a cualquier piloto estadounidense hallado con vida. Una presentadora de una filial local de la emisora estatal iraní llamó a capturar vivos a los “pilotos enemigos” y ofreció una “generosa recompensa” por entregarlos a las fuerzas de seguridad.
Según la prensa israelí, tras el derribo del F-15E las fuerzas estadounidenses activaron de inmediato la operación de rescate para intentar localizar a los tripulantes antes de que fueran encontrados por las autoridades iraníes. El medio añade que, horas después, el Canal 12 de Israel informó de que uno de los pilotos “fue aparentemente rescatado con éxito”, aunque mantuvo la cautela sobre el destino del segundo ocupante de la aeronave.
La televisión estatal iraní llamó a capturar vivos a los “pilotos enemigos” y ofreció una “generosa recompensa”
La misma publicación agrega que el Comando Central de Estados Unidos tendría desplegados grupos especializados en misiones de rescate cerca de Irán, incluidos dispositivos en Irak y Siria. Además, recoge versiones de medios vinculados a la Guardia Revolucionaria iraní según las cuales helicópteros estadounidenses participaban en la búsqueda, y una de esas aeronaves se habría retirado tras ser atacada.
Este sería el cuarto F-15 abatido desde que EE UU e Israel iniciaron sus bombardeos sobre Irán el pasado 28 de febrero. Los tres casos anteriores se produjeron en un episodio de fuego amigo en Kuwait, del que sus tripulantes pudieron ser rescatados.
El incidente marca además un nuevo salto en la llamada operación Furia Épica, nombre con el que la Administración de Donald Trump ha bautizado la ofensiva conjunta contra Teherán. Hace dos días, Trump había prometido golpear a Irán “con dureza” en las próximas dos o tres semanas. Sin embargo, en el discurso a la nación pronunciado este miércoles, el presidente no aclaró cómo se desarrollará esa fase de la ofensiva ni precisó qué ocurrirá con el estrecho de Ormuz, por donde pasa el 20% del petróleo mundial y que Teherán mantiene bloqueado.

sources.news_title: One Crew Member Of U.S. Fighter Jet Downed Over Iran Reportedly Rescued, Search Continues For Second
sources.text:
One of the two crew of U.S. fighter jet downed over Iran has been rescued by American forces, major US media outlets reported Friday after Iranian media aired footage of aircraft wreckage.
Axios and CBS News, citing unidentified sources, reported that one of the two crew on the plane had already been rescued by U.S. Special Forces (SF) but that the search was ongoing for the second crew member.
According to The New York Times and Wall Street Journal, the plane was an F-15E fighter, which is crewed by a pilot and a weapons-systems officer in the back seat.
CNN also said that analysis of what Iranian media said were photos of the wreckage showed an F-15, rather than an F-35 stealth fighter, as claimed in some Iranian reports.
US media reported that President Donald Trump had been briefed on the situation.
However, there was no immediate on-the-record response from the White House or Pentagon to requests for comment.
US media reported that a search-and-rescue operation was underway by specialized US forces, following what would be the first known loss of a jet inside Iran since Trump ordered the war.
Photos and video circulating on social media and Iranian news outlets were cited by major US media outlets as showing US helicopters and other aircraft flying at low altitude over the presumed site of the downed fighter jet.
“Military forces have launched a search operation to find the American fighter pilot who was hit earlier today,” Iran’s Fars news agency said.
“Dear and honorable people of Kohgiluyeh and Boyer-Ahmad province, if you capture the enemy pilot or pilots alive and hand them over to the police and military forces, you will receive a valuable reward and bonus,” said an Iranian television reporter on the official local channel.
The report of the downed jet came as fresh strikes hit Israel, Iran and Gulf countries.

sources.news_title: BREAKING: One of the U.S. Crew Members Rescued After F-15E Fighter Jet Shot Down Over Iran
sources.text:
BREAKING: One of the U.S. Crew Members Rescued After F-15E Fighter Jet Shot Down Over Iran
CBS News / YouTube
The Incident and Immediate Rescue
A U.S. F-15E Strike Eagle fighter jet was shot down over Iranian territory during ongoing military operations, marking a serious moment in the current conflict. According to American officials and reports confirmed by multiple news outlets, the aircraft went down after being struck by enemy fire. The two crew members aboard safely ejected before the jet crashed, beginning a dangerous race to recover them inside hostile territory.
Within hours, U.S. special operations forces launched a combat search-and-rescue mission. One of the airmen was located alive and successfully recovered by American forces. Officials said the rescued crew member was brought into U.S. custody and received medical attention soon afterward. The operation involved several aircraft working together, including rescue helicopters and refueling planes flying deep into contested airspace. The search for the second crew member continues as military planners balance urgency with safety concerns.
Search Efforts and Rising Tensions
The rescue mission unfolded while Iranian authorities conducted their own search efforts. State media encouraged civilians to report or locate the surviving crew, even announcing rewards tied to finding them. These developments increased pressure on the ongoing rescue operation, as both sides attempted to reach the missing airman first. Reports indicated that intelligence cooperation between the United States and Israel helped narrow search areas and guide recovery teams.
An Israeli official also stated that planned military strikes were delayed to avoid interfering with recovery efforts. Such pauses are rare during active operations and show how rescuing personnel often becomes the highest priority once an aircraft is lost. Combat search missions are among the most dangerous military tasks because rescue crews must enter areas where enemy defenses remain active. Videos circulating online appeared to show rescue aircraft operating at low altitude, a tactic used to avoid radar detection.
The Aircraft and Its Crew
The F-15E Strike Eagle is a two-seat fighter designed for both air-to-air combat and ground attack missions. Built by Boeing, it carries a pilot and a weapons systems officer who manages targeting and navigation during complex operations. The aircraft has served for decades as one of the U.S. Air Force’s primary strike platforms, valued for its long range and heavy payload capacity.
This incident marked the first time during the present conflict that a U.S. manned aircraft was confirmed shot down by enemy fire. Earlier in the campaign, three F-15E jets were lost in a separate friendly-fire incident, though all crew members survived those events. Military officials noted that the downing highlights the continuing risks faced by aircrews despite earlier claims that opposing air defenses had been weakened.
View this post on Instagram
Wider Context of the Conflict
The downing of the jet comes during a broader military campaign that has already resulted in American casualties and significant equipment losses. At least 13 U.S. service members have been killed and hundreds wounded since operations began, underscoring the growing human cost of the conflict. The aircraft loss also carries symbolic weight, showing that contested airspace remains dangerous even for advanced fighters.
White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt confirmed that the president had been briefed shortly after news of the incident emerged. Officials have released limited operational details, reflecting the sensitive nature of ongoing rescue efforts. Meanwhile, analysts note that the event could influence military planning moving forward, especially regarding flight routes and defensive measures for strike missions over heavily defended regions.
As search teams continue scanning remote terrain for the missing crew member, the situation remains active and uncertain. Military rescuers face time pressure, geography, and the presence of opposing forces, all while attempting to bring the remaining airman home safely.

sources.news_title: Washington Is on Red Alert! Within Hours, the Us Shot Down 2 Planes and 1 Helicopter.
sources.text:
ABD kırmızı alarmda! "Tank Avcısı" A-10 uçağı da düştü
İran’da düşürülen F-15E'nin ardından bölge tam bir ateş hattına döndü. Kurtarma helikopterleri ateş altına alındı, ABD ordusuna ait A-10 tipi savaş uçağının Basra Körfezi'nde düştüğü öne sürüldü. ABD'nin 48 saatlik acil ateşkes teklifine İran'dan "ret" cevabı gecikmezken Emekli İstihbarat Albay Coşkun Başbuğ ve Askeri Stratejist Doç. Dr. Kemal Olçar, deşifre edilen kritik teknik detayları ve sahadaki son durumu analiz etti.
İran'ın en gelişmiş Amerikan savaş uçağını vurduğu iddiası bölgeyi ateş hattına çevirirken, ABD'nin F-15 kaybını kabul etmesiyle tansiyon zirveye tırmandı.
Uçak enkazından gelen çarpıcı görüntüler, Amerikan askerlerini kurtarmak için başlatılan nefes kesen operasyon ve bir sivilin Amerikan helikopterlerine tüfekle ateş açtığı o dehşet anları kameralara yansıdı.
Emekli İstihbarat Albay Coşkun Başbuğ, bölgedeki tarihi tanıklığı ve deşifre edilen kritik teknik detayları A Haber ekranlarında tek tek analiz etti.
F-35 Mİ F-15 Mİ? ENKAZDAKİ KRİTİK İPUCU
İran ve ABD arasındaki gerilim, bir Amerikan savaş uçağının düşürülmesiyle yeni bir boyuta evrildi. İran tarafının "en iyisini vurdum" diyerek F-35 iddiasını ortaya atması, askeri çevrelerde geniş yankı buldu. Emekli İstihbarat Albay Coşkun Başbuğ, "Gün boyu takip ettik, görüntülere baktığımda F-15 olduğuna yönelik bende de bir kanaat oluştu" sözleriyle ilk analizini paylaştı. Enkaz görüntülerindeki en kritik detayın fırlatma koltuğu olduğunu belirten Başbuğ, "Bu koltuk, bir fırlatma koltuğu ve F-15'in olduğuna yönelik güçlü bir intiba oluşturdu. Görüntüleri kıyasladığımızda iki pilotlu bir F-15'in düşürüldüğü anlaşılıyor" ifadelerini kullandı.
HAYALET UÇAK EFSANESİ VE NESİL FARKI
Düşen uçağın teknik kapasitesi üzerine değerlendirmelerde bulunan Coşkun Başbuğ, "F-35 zaten 5. nesil ve hayalet olarak biliniyor, radarların yakalayamadığı bir hikaye yaratılıyor. Ama bu uçak o değil, bu bir F-15. Muhtemelen Amerikan donanmasından, yani uçak gemisinden kalkan uçakların yürüttüğü bir operasyon veya keşif gözetleme faaliyeti sırasında bu olay yaşandı" şeklinde konuştu.
İRAN HAVA SAHASINDA KURTARMA OPERASYONU
Uçağın düşmesinin ardından ABD, İran toprakları üzerinde riskli bir kurtarma operasyonu başlattı. Keş Adası üzerinde gerçekleştiği belirtilen olayda, Amerikan hava unsurlarının bölgeyi adeta abluka altına aldığı görüldü. Görüntüleri yorumlayan Coşkun Başbuğ, "Şu an bir hava harekatı düzenleniyor. Bir büyük uçağa bağlı iki helikopter görüyoruz, adeta hava ikmali yapılıyor. İki adet Black Hawk, yani bizdeki adıyla Sikorsky, pilotları alma adına hava harekatı düzenliyor. Tanker uçak da bu helikopterlere eşlik ederek havada yakıt ikmali sağlıyor" dedi.
SİVİL ÇİFTÇİDEN AMERİKAN HELİKOPTERİNE ATEŞ ANLARI
Operasyon sırasında kaydedilen bir görüntü, savaşın en çıplak yüzünü ortaya koydu. Bir İranlı sivilin, ailesi ve çocuklarının yanındayken Amerikan helikopterlerine kişisel tüfeğiyle ateş açması kameralara yansıdı. Bu anları değerlendiren Coşkun Başbuğ, "Görüntüde bir kişi var, ailesi yanında, eline almış bir tüfek ve Amerikan hava unsuruna ateş ediyor. Bu size tuhaf gelmesin, Irak işgalinde de birebir gördüm; bir çiftçi elindeki çifteyle Amerikan helikopterini yere indirmişti ve o olay çok tartışılmıştı. Şimdi benzer bir tablo İran'da yaşanıyor" sözleriyle tarihi bir benzerliğe dikkat çekti.
İRAN'IN HAVA SAVUNMA SIRRI: RUSYA VEYA ÇİN DESTEĞİ Mİ?
ABD uçaklarının vurulması, "İran bu teknolojiye nasıl ulaştı?" sorusunu da beraberinde getirdi. Coşkun Başbuğ, bu konudaki şüpheleri, "İran'ın hava sahası daha önce yol geçen hanına dönmüştü, İsrail ve ABD çok rahat hareket ediyordu. Ama şimdi ne oldu da bu başarı bir anda ortaya çıktı? Çin'in desteği mi yoksa Rusya'dan S-300 gibi teknik sistemlerin desteği mi alındı? Bu bilgiler teyide muhtaç ama bir gerçek var ki; uçaklar vurulabiliyor" şeklinde ifade etti.
SUUDİ ARABİSTAN'DA VE KUVEYT'TE HELİKOPTER HAREKETLİLİĞİ
Sıcak temasın sadece İran ile sınırlı kalmadığı, Suudi Arabistan hava sahasında da hareketli saatler yaşandığı iddia edildi. Coşkun Başbuğ, "Bugün İran, üç Amerikan hava unsurunu vurduğunu açıkladı. Suudi Arabistan hava sahasında bir F-16'nın vurulduğu ve oraya iniş yaptığı bilgisi var. Ayrıca Kuveyt'te bir helikopterin vurulduğu söyleniyor. ABD bunlardan ikisini kabul etti" diyerek çatışmanın coğrafi olarak genişlediğini vurguladı.
PİLOTLARIN AKIBETİ: BİRİ KURTARILDI, DİĞERİ KAYIP
Operasyonun en kritik aşaması olan pilotların durumu hakkında ise çelişkili bilgiler gelmeye devam ediyor. Coşkun Başbuğ, uluslararası basına yansıyan son bilgileri, "İran'ın güneyinde bir pilota canlı olarak ulaşıldığı ve kurtarıldığı bilgisi Amerikan basınında, CNN ve CBS gibi kanallarda yer aldı. Ancak uçakta iki pilot olduğunu biliyoruz. Diğer pilot nerede? Henüz ulaşılmadı mı yoksa İranlı yetkililer mi onu buldu? Bu sorunun cevabını ilerleyen dakikalarda göreceğiz" ifadeleriyle aktardı.
STRATEJİK ZAAFİYET TARTIŞMASI
ABD'nin bölgedeki rahatlığının sorgulanması gerektiğini belirten Başbuğ, "Eğer İran'ın elinde F-35 veya F-15 düşürecek bir sistem varsa, bu helikopterler nasıl bu kadar rahat operasyon yapabiliyor? Sınırlı sayıda mı sistem var yoksa bir hava zafiyeti mi söz konusu? Bu sorular hala cevapsız" diyerek bölgedeki askeri belirsizliğin altını çizdi.

【大紀元2026年04月03日訊】（大紀元記者林燕報導）美東時間週五（4月3日）早上11點多，美國官員證實，一架美國F-15E戰機在伊朗上空被擊落，美軍正在展開救援行動。該機有兩名機組人員，最新消息是，已有一名人員獲救。
這是伊朗在本次戰爭中首次擊落美國的有人駕駛飛機。
白宮證實，川普（特朗普）總統已經聽取該事件的簡報。白宮新聞發言人卡羅琳‧萊維特（Karoline Leavitt）告訴美國有線電視新聞網（CNN），總統已聽取了今早美國戰機在伊朗上空被擊落的簡報。
第一名飛行員的獲救細節
美東時間下午4:10，兩名美國官員告訴CBS新聞，在伊朗上空被擊落後獲救的美國F-15E戰機飛行員是由兩架美國軍用直升機救起的。
對另一名F-15E機組人員——一名武器系統操作員——的搜尋仍在繼續。
載著獲救飛行員的美方直升機遭到伊朗的輕武器射擊，導致機上機組人員中有人受傷。隨後直升機安全著陸。所有服役人員均已接受初步醫療救治，並將送往醫院接受進一步治療。
有兩架美方直升機遭伊朗炮火襲擊
美東時間下午3:30，據美國全國廣播公司（NBC）引述一位美國官員的消息說，兩架美軍直升機在搜尋被擊落戰鬥機兩名機組人員的過程中，遭到伊朗炮火襲擊。
該官員表示，「所有軍人均安全」。
消息：第二名機組人員有取得聯繫
美東時間下午2點，以色列第12頻道引述知情人士的消息稱，兩名美軍機組人員在戰鬥機被擊中後安全彈射。飛行員在與美國陸軍取得初步聯繫後被找到，而後座機組人員（武器系統操作員）稍後也已取得聯繫，目前仍在搜尋中。
此外，美國媒體Newsmax引述知情人士的消息說，一架美國黑鷹直升機在伊朗上空執行營救第二名F-15機組人員的任務時遭到襲擊，但成功安全離開伊朗領空並安全著陸，未發生其他意外。
以色列官員：對第二名機組人員的搜尋仍在進行
以色列高級安全官員向《大紀元》雜誌以色列版證實，一架美國飛機在伊朗領空被擊落。
官員們透露，美國已向墜機地點派遣搜救隊，目前已成功救出一名飛行員。此外，對另一名機組人員的搜尋仍在進行中。
一名飛行員獲救
以色列第12頻道最早報導說，已有一名美國機組人員成功獲救。
隨後美國官員證實，被擊落的F-15E戰機上的一名美國機組人員獲救。
兩名美國官員告訴哥倫比亞廣播公司新聞網（CBS News），一架在伊朗上空被擊落的美國F-15E戰鬥機上的一名機組人員已被美軍救起。
CBS新聞報導，兩名消息人士證實，搜救行動正在進行中。
消息：美特種部隊在伊朗境內救回一名機組人員
Axios引述知情人士的消息稱，兩名機組人員在被伊朗炮火擊中後安全彈射逃生。
報導說，美國特種部隊在伊朗境內找到了其中一名機組人員並將其救起，該機組人員還活著。
一位以色列官員表示，以色列取消了原定在伊朗的空襲計劃，以免干擾搜救行動。
F-15E戰鬥機介紹
F-15E是雙座戰機。
F-15最初是一款空對空戰鬥機。F-15E是一款具備空對地攻擊能力的多用途戰鬥機。後座機組人員是一名武器系統操作員。
網絡上流傳多個美軍救援行動視頻
社交媒體上流傳著一些照片和視頻，伊朗官方媒體也分享了這些照片和視頻，顯示至少有一架美國C-130運輸機和兩架黑鷹直升機在伊朗中部和西南部低空飛行，據稱這可能是為了搜尋和營救被擊落的美軍人員。
CBS新聞國家安全分析師亞倫‧麥克萊恩（Aaron MacLean）表示，社交媒體和伊朗國家媒體廣泛傳播的畫面顯示，美國戰機和武裝直升機於週五低空飛行，這與典型的搜救任務行動相符。
他表示，視頻片段中出現的飛機（CBS新聞已獨立核實部分片段）似乎在光天化日之下低空飛越敵對領空，而美軍只有在有充分理由的情況下才會這樣做，例如營救被擊落的飛行員。
伊朗當局懸賞要求活捉美飛行員
墜機事件發生在伊朗西部。據伊朗媒體報導，美軍正在兩處墜落地點搜尋這兩名飛行員。
伊朗電視台也宣布，懸賞100億圖曼（約64,102美元）尋找失蹤飛行員。
伊朗官方呼籲民眾參與搜尋行動，抓捕這兩名美軍飛行員，要留活口。
以色列陸軍電台援引以色列消息人士的話也證實了這架戰機被擊落的消息，並表示搜救行動正在進行中。目前尚不清楚機組人員的情況。
與伊朗安全部門關係密切的法爾斯通訊社發布了據稱是墜毀戰機殘骸的照片。

sources.news_title: Iran Shoots Down the First F-15e u.s. Fighter over Its Territory
sources.text:
Irán ha derribado un caza estadounidense en su territorio por primera vez desde que EEUU e Israel iniciaron la guerra contra la República Islámica, según han informado funcionarios de EEUU y medios afines a Teherán a varios medios estadounidenses este viernes.
El derribo del avión de combate, que sería un F-15E de la Fuerza Aérea, tuvo lugar al sur de Irán, según medios como el diario ‘The Washington Post’.
Poco después de iniciar una misión para rescatar a los dos tripulantes que iban a bordo, Washington consiguió recuperar al menos a uno de ellos, que está vivo y se encuentra recibiendo atención médica, según ha informado CNN.
Sin embargo, no está clara la situación del otro tripulante, aunque las operaciones de búsqueda siguen en marcha, ha indicado a Axios un funcionario israelí y una segunda fuente con conocimiento de la situación.
Este sería el cuarto F-15 atacado desde que EEUU e Israel iniciaron los ataques contra Irán el pasado 28 de febrero. Los otros tres ocurrieron, según Washington, en un incidente de fuego amigo en Kuwait al inicio de las hostilidades, pero los tripulantes fueron rescatados.
El derribo en territorio iraní supone un nuevo paso de la operación Furia Épica, como bautizó la Administración de Donald Trump al operativo conjunto contra Teherán, después de que, hace dos días, el mandatario prometiera atacarle «con dureza» durante las próximas dos o tres semanas.
Trump ofreció un discurso a la nación este miércoles en el que, lejos de declarar el fin de la guerra, no concretó detalles de cómo se llevarán a cabo las, supuestas, últimas semanas de conflicto, ni de la apertura del estrecho de Ormuz, que ha obligado a países de todo el globo a tomar medidas urgentes contra el desabastecimiento energético.
Las purgas de Trump
El Departamento de Guerra de EEUU ordenó este jueves al jefe del Estado Mayor, Randy George, retirarse de su cargo de forma inmediata.
George, encargado de organizar las fuerzas de tierra del Ejército estadounidense, fue cesado de su cargo por el secretario de Guerra, Pete Hegseth, luego de haber estado a cargo desde agosto de 2023, de acuerdo con el vocero del departamento, Sean Parnell.
Parnell, confirmó el retiro de George asegurando en su cuenta de X que: «El general Randy A. George se retirará de su cargo como el 41.º Jefe de Estado Mayor del Ejército con efecto inmediato».
Además, el general David Hodne, jefe del Comando de Transformación y Entrenamiento, así como el mayor William Green, jefe del Cuerpo de Capellanes, también habrían sido relevados, de acuerdo con el ‘The Washington Post’
Medios estadounidenses como CBS y CNN informaron previamente que George ha tenido una relación conflictiva con el secretario Hegseth y otros altos mandos en medio del conflicto de Irán por la toma de decisiones.
George, oficial de infantería de carrera, se graduó como oficial en la Academia Militar de los EEUU en West Point en 1988.
Ha ejercido como jefe de Estado Mayor desde septiembre de 2023; anteriormente comandó el I Cuerpo en la Base Conjunta Lewis-McChord y posteriormente fue asistente militar principal del Secretario de Defensa Lloyd Austin durante la administración de Joe Biden.
A las purgas en el Estado Mayor se suma la de la Fiscal General, Pam Bondi, a quien Trump destituyó este jueves despúes de semanas mostrando frustración con el liderazgo de la abogada, a quien reprochaba una supuesta falta de agresividad a la hora de perseguir a sus adversarios políticos, así como su controvertida gestión de los archivos del caso Epstein.
Economía de guerra
Trump afirmó este jueves que ha determinado que el presupuesto militar del país para 2027 debería incrementarse en un 50% hasta alcanzar 1,5 billones de dólares, un máximo histórico que el republicano considera que puede financiarse gracias a los aranceles.
En una publicación de Truth Social, Trump aseguró que este presupuesto, que logrará construir el «sueño militar» del país, será financiado por medio de los aranceles impuestos a otros países. El que será el presupuesto más alto en la historia de las fuerzas armadas de EEUU fue aprobado tras una «larga y difícil serie de negociaciones con senadores, secretarios y otros representantes políticos», aseguró el mandatario.

sources.news_title: U.S. F-15E Strike Eagle Shot Down Over Southern Iran: One Pilot Rescued Behind Enemy Lines, Second Crew Member Missing
sources.text:
*As Iran Urges Civilians to Hunt Down Americans
An American F-15E Strike Eagle — a two-seater fighter jet that costs approximately $100 million — has been shot down over southern Iran, two U.S. officials confirmed. The aircraft appears to have been shot down by Iran, and the American military immediately launched a search and rescue operation for those on board.
The incident marks the first time a U.S. jet has been downed by enemy fire since the start of the war, now more than a month old and into its 35th day. It represents a major escalation in the conflict and adds to doubts over American-Israeli claims of dominance over Iran’s skies.
Iranian state media published photos alongside claims from the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) that it had shot down the aircraft. The Pentagon and the White House did not immediately comment on the Iranian claims.
Nour News, an outlet linked to the Revolutionary Guard, claimed the jet was destroyed by Iran’s own advanced military technology.
“The jet was destroyed in the skies over central Iran by a new advanced air defence system of the IRGC Aerospace Force.”
Iranian media released images showing debris as well as ejector seats from the downed F-15E. The regime has previously made a series of false claims about shooting down piloted U.S. planes, but this was the first time state media called on the public to actively search for suspected American pilots, suggesting the regime believed the incident was genuine.
Iran had claimed previously to have struck American military planes during the war, but the U.S. had not confirmed any such incidents prior to this.
Responding to photos published by outlets in Tehran, one expert identified the aircraft as an F-15 based on its structure.
“Structure looks like an F-15. From the tail flash stripe markings from the 48th Fighter Wing, based at RAF Lakenheath in the United Kingdom.”
The base at RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk, eastern England, and RAF Feltwell in the neighbouring county of Norfolk host the 48th Fighter Wing, comprising some 7,000 active-duty personnel and four squadrons of F-15 Strike Eagles and F-35A Lightning II fighter jets. It is the largest U.S. fighter operation in Europe and has been a key hub of American activity heading to the Middle East.
An American fighter pilot has been rescued by U.S. forces after being shot down behind enemy lines, two U.S. officials confirmed. The rescue mission followed hours of reporting by Iranian state media of a downed U.S. fighter jet.
However, a second crew member from the two-seater F-15E Strike Eagle remains missing. The American military was conducting a search for the missing crew member in what is an intensely rural and mountainous region of southwestern Iran.
White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt confirmed that President Donald Trump had been briefed on the incident, describing it as the latest dramatic development in the war.
In a chilling development, Iranian state media called on civilians in the rural and mountainous region of southern Iran to actively hunt down the American pilots. A channel affiliated with Iranian state television claimed that a U.S. pilot had ejected from their aircraft over a rural region of southwestern Iran.
An anchor on the channel urged local residents to hand over any “enemy pilot” to police and promised a reward for anyone who did. The local television channel is based in Kohkilouyeh and Boyer-Ahmad province, an intensely rural and mountainous region.
In an even more alarming escalation, an on-screen crawl on Iranian state media urged the public to “shoot them if you see them,” referring to videos circulating of what appeared to be U.S. aircraft flying low in the area, apparently conducting the search and rescue mission.
A regional governor in Iran’s southwest issued a public plea for locals to find those on board the jet and promised a reward. A representative of merchants and businesses was reportedly offering the equivalent of $60,000 for information leading to the capture of the pilots.
The situation on the ground became even more dangerous as footage emerged of tribesmen shooting at what appeared to be American search and rescue aircraft. The semiofficial Mehr news agency published videos that it said showed “brave locals firing at U.S. helicopters” with guns.
Separate videos purported to show U.S. military aircraft involved in the rescue operation, including an Air Force HC-130J Combat King II, a specialised search and rescue plane; a U.S. KC-130 refuelling tanker; and two HH-60 Pave Hawk search and rescue helicopters.
The footage of armed civilians firing at American rescue aircraft underscored the extreme danger facing the search and rescue teams operating deep behind enemy lines in hostile terrain.
The shootdown came as President Trump had declared success and was pressuring Iran to agree to a deal to end the war, while simultaneously massing new troops in the Middle East and threatening intense escalation if Tehran does not reopen the vital Strait of Hormuz trade route.
Trump had vowed during an address to the nation on Wednesday night to wind down the conflict in the coming weeks. The loss of the F-15E complicates that narrative and raises questions about the trajectory of the war.
The joint U.S.-Israeli campaign has focused intensely on destroying and degrading Iran’s missile defences, but the shootdown demonstrated that Tehran has retained the capability to hit back across the region. The incident will add to doubts over American-Israeli claims of dominance over Iran’s skies.
As the war entered its 35th day, Iran launched new attacks on Gulf energy sites, with strikes on a desalination plant and oil refinery in Kuwait as well as a gas complex in Abu Dhabi. The attacks on critical civilian infrastructure in neighbouring Gulf states underscored the widening scope of the conflict and Iran’s willingness to strike beyond its own borders.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu claimed that most of Iran’s steel production capacity had been destroyed after the U.S. and Israel targeted industrial facilities. In a new video, Netanyahu detailed the scale of the joint military campaign.
“Together with our American friends, we continue to crush the terror regime in Iran. We are eliminating commanders, bombing bridges, bombing infrastructure. In recent days, the Air Force has destroyed 70% of Iran’s steel production capacity. This is a tremendous achievement that deprives the Revolutionary Guards of both financial sources and the ability to produce a large number of weapons.”
“In full coordination between myself and President Trump, between the IDF and the United States Army, we will continue to crush Iran. This regime is weaker than ever — Israel is stronger than ever.”
Key Facts at a Glance
- Aircraft: F-15E Strike Eagle (two-seater, approximately $100 million)
- Unit: 48th Fighter Wing, based at RAF Lakenheath, United Kingdom
- Location: Shot down over southern Iran (Kohkilouyeh and Boyer-Ahmad province)
- Crew Status: One pilot rescued behind enemy lines; one crew member still missing
- Iran’s Claim: IRGC says it used a “new advanced air defence system”
- Significance: First U.S. jet downed by enemy fire since the war began (Day 35)
- Reward Offered: Equivalent of $60,000 offered by merchants for information on pilots
- Rescue Aircraft Spotted: HC-130J Combat King II, KC-130 refuelling tanker, two HH-60 Pave Hawk helicopters
- Trump: Briefed on incident; had vowed to wind down conflict in coming weeks
- Iran’s Gulf Strikes: Strikes on desalination plant and oil refinery in Kuwait; gas complex in Abu Dhabi
- Netanyahu: Claims 70% of Iran’s steel production capacity destroyed by joint U.S.-Israel campaign

sources.text:
Seit dem 28. Februar gibt es erneut Krieg im Nahen Osten: An diesem Tag griffen die USA und Israel Iran an. Gleich am ersten Tag gelang es ihnen dabei, Ajatollah Ali Chamenei, den obersten Führer Irans, sowie weitere Mitglieder der Führung des Landes zu töten. Doch anders, als von den USA geplant, kommt es nicht zu einem schnellen Sieg. Iran reagierte mit Gegenangriffen auf Israel und viele Golfstaaten sowie dortige US-Militärbasen – und blockiert die für den weltweiten Ölhandel wichtige Straße von Hormus. Alle Infos zur Lage in Iran und in der kompletten Region finden Sie im Live-Ticker:
US-Präsident Donald Trump hatte kurz nach den ersten Militäraktionen davon gesprochen, dass es bei dem Krieg um die Sicherheit der USA gehe. Er sprach von einer Gefahr durch das iranische Raketenprogramm und erklärte, dass verhindert werden müsse, dass Iran eine Atombombe entwickeln könne. Israel begründet sein Vorgehen mit einer existenziellen Bedrohung durch das iranische Regime. Kritiker halten das Vorgehen von den USA und Israel für völkerrechtswidrig.
Trump drohte Iran nach gewaltsamer Niederschlagung von Protesten
Schon Wochen zuvor hatte Trump dem Regime Irans gedroht, als dieses zu Beginn des Jahres Massenproteste gewaltvoll niederschlug. Millionen Iranerinnen und Iraner hatten auf den Straßen gegen das Mullah-Regime demonstriert. Da das Internet zwischenzeitlich abgeschaltet worden war, gab es kaum gesicherte Informationen, doch es gibt Berichte über mehrere tausend getötete Demonstranten.
Ebenfalls am Krieg beteiligt ist die von Iran unterstützte Terrororganisation Hisbollah im Libanon. Diese beschießt Israel, das wiederum Ziele im Libanon angreift und auch mit Bodentruppen in dem Nachbarland vorrückt.
Straße von Hormus blockiert: Ölpreis steigt infolge des Krieges in Iran
Der Krieg hat auch Folgen auf die Weltwirtschaft, insbesondere auf den Ölpreis. Das liegt unter anderem daran, dass Iran die Straße von Hormus blockiert – eine Meerenge im Persischen Golf, durch die normalerweise rund ein Fünftel des weltweit gehandelten Öls transportiert wird. (mit dpa)

sources.news_title: One US Pilot rescued after Iran downs Fighter Jet over hostile skies
sources.text:
One US Pilot rescued after Iran downs Fighter Jet over hostile skies
Quick Read
One crew member from a US Air Force F-15E Strike Eagle fighter jet shot down over Iran has been successfully rescued by American forces, two US officials told CBS News on Friday.
By Kazeem Ugbodaga
One crew member from a US Air Force F-15E Strike Eagle fighter jet shot down over Iran has been successfully rescued by American forces, two US officials told CBS News on Friday.
A search and rescue operation continues for the second crew member.
White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt confirmed that President Donald Trump has been briefed on the incident.
“The President has been briefed,” she stated, without providing further details on the timing or content of the update.
The downing of the twin-seat F-15E marks the first time a US combat aircraft has been lost to Iranian air defenses over Iranian territory since the current conflict began nearly five weeks ago.
The jet was operating in or near Khuzestan Province in southwestern Iran when it was brought down.
US forces launched an immediate combat search and rescue mission following the incident. Video footage previously geolocated to the area showed low-flying aircraft and helicopters consistent with rescue and support operations near the Karoon River.
Iranian state media had reported that initial searches for ejected crew members were unsuccessful and offered rewards for the capture of any “enemy pilots.”
The successful rescue of at least one aviator represents a partial victory for US recovery efforts in contested airspace, though the status of the second crew member remains unknown.
Officials have not disclosed details on the condition of the rescued individual or the exact circumstances of the extraction.
The Pentagon and US Central Command have not issued an official statement on the shoot-down or the ongoing operation as of late Friday. The incident comes amid broader US military actions against Iranian targets, including recent strikes on infrastructure.
Earlier in the conflict, three US F-15Es were lost in a friendly-fire incident involving Kuwaiti air defenses, with all crew safely ejecting. Iranian claims initially referenced an F-35 in some reports, but US sources and visual evidence have consistently identified the aircraft as an F-15E.

Key Points
- The rescued individual is reportedly alive and has been placed in US custody and receiving medical treatment.
- The search and rescue effort followed initial reports from multiple news outlets, including The Wall Street Journal, confirming the aircraft was shot down.
- Technical details provided by a US source confirmed that the downed plane was an F-15E Strike Eagle fighter jet.
The rescued individual is reportedly alive and has been placed "in US custody and receiving medical treatment," as confirmed by two of the sources.

Technical details provided by a US source confirmed that the downed plane was an "F-15E Strike Eagle fighter jet." This specific model is a dual-role aircraft designed to execute both "air-to-air and air-to-ground missions."
As noted by CNN, these aircraft are traditionally operated by a two-person team consisting of a pilot and a weapon systems officer. Military officials continue to monitor the situation as the search for the remaining personnel persists.

CNN's analysis of images released by Iranian media verified that the wreckage matches an F-15, while The Wall Street Journal cited Iranian state broadcaster IRIB, which first reported on Friday that the jet had been targeted.

While the exact crash site remains unconfirmed, CNN geolocated footage from a bridge over the Karoon River in Khuzestan Province, roughly 470 km south of Tehran, showing low-flying aircraft and helicopters in a formation typical of air-to-air refuelling operations.
This incident marks the first time a US aircraft has been downed over Iran during the current conflict. US outlet Axios also confirmed the rescue mission was underway, as Iranian media began circulating photographs of debris, including a tail fin, which appeared to identify the jet as belonging to the 494th Fighter Squadron 'LN' based at RAF Lakenheath in the United Kingdom.

sources.news_title: Us Fighter Jet Shot Down over Iran. Search and Rescue Operation
sources.text:
Iran twierdził, że samolot pochodził z 48. Skrzydła Myśliwskiego USA, które stacjonuje na co dzień w bazie lotniczej Lakenheath w Wielkiej Brytanii i dysponuje myśliwcami F-15E oraz F-35A. Następnie irańska telewizja państwowa pokazała rzekome zdjęcia zestrzelonego myśliwca sił powietrznych USA, z których wynika, że jest to najpewniej maszyna typu F-15E.
Irańskie media wzywały do "polowania" na pilota
Do upadku maszyny miało dojść w położonej w centrum Iranu prowincji Markazi, na południowy zachód od Teheranu, stolicy kraju. Agencja Fars poinformowała, że myśliwiec został "całkowicie zniszczony i rozbił się".
Agencja Mehr podała, że mało prawdopodobne jest, aby pilotowi udało się katapultować ze względu na "gwałtowną eksplozję", do której doszło w wyniku katastrofy. Mimo tego, irańska telewizja wezwała cywilów do pomocy w "schwytaniu" pilota.
CBS News podało przed godz. 18, że członek załogi amerykańskiego myśliwca F-15E został uratowany przez siły amerykańskie. O sprawie poinformowało dwóch amerykańskich urzędników.
Doniesienia mediów. Armia USA milczy
W sieci pojawiło się także nagranie z akcji poszukiwawczej myśliwca.
Zestrzelenie myśliwca USA potwierdził amerykański urzędnik w rozmowie z Reutersem. Chciał jednak zachować anonimowość i nie ujawnił więcej szczegółów. Pentagon i armia USA nadal milczą na temat incydentu.

sources.news_title: u.s. Military Aircraft Shot Down in Iran: Rescue a Pilot and Search for the Second
sources.text:
Avión militar de EE. UU. derribado en Irán: un piloto fue rescatado y el otro sigue desaparecido
Se está llevando a cabo una operación de búsqueda y rescate para localizar a dos miembros de la tripulación
Según los informes, un miembro de la tripulación fue rescatado y continúa la búsqueda del segundo piloto después de que un avión de combate F-15 estadounidense fuera derribado sobre Irán.
El miembro de la tripulación fue rescatado por las fuerzas estadounidenses, según informaron dos funcionarios estadounidenses a CBS News. Asimismo, dos fuentes compartieron a CNN que el piloto rescatado se encuentra con vida y está recibiendo atención médica.
Las autoridades afirman que el piloto del F-15E Strike Eagle se eyectó antes de que el avión se estrellara. Las autoridades estadounidenses están en una carrera contra el tiempo para recuperar al segundo miembro de la tripulación antes de que las fuerzas iraníes lo encuentren. En imágenes difundidas en las redes sociales se veían drones, aviones y helicópteros estadounidenses sobrevolando la región montañosa.
Un presentador de noticias iraní instó a los residentes a entregar a cualquier “piloto enemigo” a la policía y prometió una recompensa a quien lo hiciera. Un mensaje en pantalla instaba anteriormente al público a “dispararles si los ven”, refiriéndose a las imágenes que circulaban en las redes sociales de lo que parecían ser aviones estadounidenses en la zona.
Los medios de comunicación vinculados al Estado iraní informaron que se habían desplegado helicópteros para buscar a la tripulación del avión accidentado, aunque las versiones sobre su procedencia eran contradictorias.
La agencia de noticias Fars afirmó que no estaba claro quién pilotaba el avión, mientras que Tasnim informó que eran estadounidenses y detalló que al menos un helicóptero se vio obligado a retirarse tras ser atacado. Tasnim también señaló que un avión C-130 Hércules de EE. UU. participó en la operación.
Mizan, un medio afiliado al poder judicial iraní, informó que estaba en marcha una misión de rescate estadounidense y publicó imágenes que, según afirmó, mostraban aviones estadounidenses en el espacio aéreo iraní.
Según Reuters, las autoridades iraníes pidieron a la población civil que estuviera atenta a la búsqueda de sobrevivientes. El gobernador de la provincia iraní de Kohgiluyeh y Boyer-Ahmad afirmó que quien capturara o matara a la tripulación “recibiría un reconocimiento especial”, según la agencia de noticias semioficial iraní ISNA.
El presidente Donald Trump fue informado de los acontecimientos, que se producen en un momento en el que la tensión entre Estados Unidos e Irán sigue escalando. En las últimas 24 horas, ambas partes han intercambiado ataques contra infraestructuras militares y civiles en toda la región.
El incidente podría suponer una complicación política significativa para Trump, quien sugirió en un discurso a la nación en horario de máxima audiencia esta semana que la guerra estaba terminando y que la capacidad militar de Irán había quedado prácticamente destruida. No obstante, afirmó que los bombardeos de Estados Unidos e Israel continuarían durante “dos o tres semanas”.
Poco antes de que el avión fuera derribado el viernes, Trump publicó en Truth Social:
“Con un poco más de tiempo, podríamos fácilmente ABRIR EL ESTRECHO DE ORMUZ, APODERARNOS DEL PETRÓLEO Y HACER UNA FORTUNA. ¿SERÍA UNA “FUENTE INAGOTABLE” PARA EL MUNDO? (sic) Presidente DONALD J. TRUMP”.
Trump ha amenazado con una mayor escalada y ha advertido posibles ataques contra la red energética de Irán si no se reabre el estrecho. Las autoridades iraníes han rechazado las negociaciones en las condiciones actuales.
“¡Los puentes serán los siguientes, luego las centrales eléctricas!”, escribió en las redes sociales el jueves por la noche. “¡Los líderes del nuevo régimen saben lo que hay que hacer, y hay que hacerlo, ¡RÁPIDO!”.
El viernes, Trump celebró el bombardeo de un puente iraní y advirtió en las redes sociales que hay “mucho más por venir”. Las imágenes mostraban el momento en que el puente B1 en Karaj, al oeste de Teherán, quedó partido a la mitad tras el ataque del jueves. El ataque dejó ocho muertos y 95 heridos, según informaron los medios de comunicación iraníes.
El incidente de hoy es el primero en el que un avión estadounidense o israelí ha sido derribado sobre Irán desde que comenzó el conflicto. Tres aviones F-15E Strike Eagle de EE. UU. fueron derribados por fuego amigo sobre Kuwait en marzo. Ningún miembro de las tripulaciones resultó herido.
Más de 1.900 personas han perdido la vida en Irán desde que comenzó la guerra el 28 de febrero con los ataques de Estados Unidos e Israel, según informó Associated Press. En un informe publicado el viernes, la organización estadounidense Armed Conflict Location and Event Data (ACLED) señaló que las víctimas civiles se concentraban en torno a ataques contra instalaciones de seguridad y vinculadas al Estado, “más que en bombardeos indiscriminados” de zonas urbanas.
Más de dos docenas de personas han muerto en los Estados del Golfo y en la Cisjordania ocupada, se han reportado 19 muertos en Israel y han fallecido 13 miembros de las fuerzas armadas estadounidenses. Más de 1.300 personas han perdido la vida y más de un millón han sido desplazadas en el Líbano. También han muerto allí diez soldados israelíes.
Traducción de Michelle Padilla

sources.news_title: Pilot Rescued After Us Fighter Jet Shot Down
sources.text:
Iran: Droneangrep mot et Israel-tilknyttet skip i Hormuzstredet
Iran: Droneangrep mot et Israel-tilknyttet skip i HormuzstredetEt israelsk-tilknyttet skip begynte å brenne etter at det ble rammet av et iransk droneangrep i Hormuzstredet lørdag, ifølge Iran.
Det opplyser Revolusjonsgarden i Iran.
– En drone traff skipet, som er tilknyttet til det sionistiske regimet, i Hormuzstredet. Skipet begynte å brenne, sier Revolusjonsgardens sjøforsvar i en uttalelse.
Det er foreløpig ukjent hvorvidt noen ble skadet i angrepet. Israel har foreløpig ikke kommentert angrepet.
Irak stenger grenseovergang til Iran
Irak stenger grenseovergang til IranEt luftangrep i området like over på iransk side førte til at en irakisk sivil borger ble drept, ifølge sikkerhetskildene.
Minst fem andre irakere ble kritisk såret i angrepet, som rammet et oppholdsområde for folk som krysser grensen.
Grenseovergangen er nå blitt stengt både for personer og for handel, ifølge irakiske myndigheter.
Luftangrepet ble utført av USA og Israel, skriver iranske medier.
Flere drept i amerikansk-israelsk angrep nær iransk atomkraftverk
Et eldre bilde av atomkraftverket i Bushehr.Flere drept i amerikansk-israelsk angrep nær iransk atomkraftverkUSA og Israel angrep lørdag et industriområde sørvest i Iran, nær et atomkraftverk. Minst fem personer skal være drept.
Minst fem personer ble drept i angrep mot de petrokjemiske anleggene i byen Mahshahr, ifølge statlige iranske medier. Tidligere lørdag meldte Det internasjonale atomenergibyrået (IAEA) at én person var drept og fem var såret.
Det statlige nyhetsbyrået Fars meldte om flere eksplosjoner ved anlegget.
IAEA opplyste at de var informert av iranske myndigheter om at angrepet var nær ved
Pilot reddet etter at amerikansk jagerfly ble skutt ned
Pilot reddet etter at amerikansk jagerfly ble skutt nedEt amerikansk jagerfly ble skutt ned over Iran fredag. Én av pilotene er reddet, ifølge kilder til flere medier.
USAs president Donald Trump er informert om at et amerikansk jagerfly er skutt ned over Iran, sier talsperson Karoline Leavitt i Det hvite hus ifølge BBC.
Dette er dermed den første kjente nedskytingen av et amerikansk kampfly over Iran siden startet av krigen i slutten av februar.
Én av pilotene er reddet, bekrefter to amerikanske kilder overfor CBS News. Også israelske medier, deriblant Jerusalem Post , viser til israelske kilder på opplysningene om at en person er reddet.
Revolusjonsgarden i Iran sa fredag at jagerflyet ble skutt ned i deres luftrom av et nytt og avansert luftvernsystem.
Paven med sterk oppfordring til Israel
Pave Leo holdt gudstjeneste i Roma skjærtorsdag. Langfredag snakket han med flere statsledere tilknyttet både krigen i Ukraina og Midtøsten. Foto: Andrew Medichini / AP / NTBPaven med sterk oppfordring til IsraelPave Leo oppfordrer Israels president om å «gjenåpne alle muligheter for dialog» for å avslutte krigen mot Iran.
Paven oppfordret Israels president Isaac Herzog til dette i en telefonsamtale langfredag.
Paven har markert seg som en sterk kritiker av konflikten i Midtøsten. Han oppfordret også Herzog til å beskytte sivile og fremme respekt for folkerett og humanitærrett.
Fransk containerskip skal ha gått gjennom Hormuzstredet
Data fra Marine Traffic viser skipets rute. Skipet seilte fra farvann utenfor Dubai mot Iran torsdag ettermiddag. Nå befinner det seg utenfor Oman. Foto: Marine Traffic / SkjermbildeFransk containerskip skal ha gått gjennom HormuzstredetDet melder nyhetsbyrået Reuters, som siterer den franske nyhetskanalen BFM TV. Skipet skal være eid av containerrederiet CMA CGM, som også eier den franske nyhetskanalen BFM TV. Reuters har ikke lykkes i å få en kommentar fra rederiet.
Skipet det skal dreier seg om er CMA CGM Kribi, ifølge Bloomberg. Data fra Marine Traffic, som leverer sanntidsinformasjon om posisjonen til skip, viser at skipet seilte fra farvann utenfor Dubai mot Iran torsdag ettermiddag lokal tid. Nå befinner det skipet utenfor Oman, ifølge sanntidsdataene.
Hormuzstredet har i praksis vært stengt for skipsfart siden USA og Israel angrep Iran 28. februar. Kun få skip er sluppet gjennom av Iran. Blokaden av Hormuzstredet har påvirket omtrent en femtedel av verdens globale energiforsyning.
Regimet i Iran har tidligere uttalt at Hormuzstredet er stengt for skiptilknyttet USA og Israel og deres støttespillere, men åpent for skip fra andre land
Brann på raffineri i Kuwait etter droneangrep
Foto: AP / NTBBrann på raffineri i Kuwait etter droneangrepRaffineriet Mina al-Ahmadi i Kuwait ble truffet i et droneangrep natt til fredag. Angrepet utløste brann på anlegget, melder statlige medier i Kuwait, som siterer Kuwait Petroleum Corporation.
Det er ikke meldt om at personer er rammet i angrepet. Brannmannskaper jobber med å slukke brannene. Det er tredje gang dette raffineriet angripes under krigen, skriver BBC.
Det er ett av Kuwaits tre store raffinerier og det ble midlertidig stengt etter angrep for to uker siden. Selskapet har nå sagt at det blir stengt i lengre tid.
I tillegg er et avsaltingsanlegg truffet. Det renser sjøvann til drikkevann. I Midtøsten kommer rundt 90 prosent av drikkevannet fra slike anlegg, ifølge BBC.
Iran hevder å ha skutt ned amerikansk jagerfly
Foto: Michel Euler / AP / NTBIran hevder å ha skutt ned amerikansk jagerflyIran hevder å ha skutt ned et amerikansk jagerfly over sentrale deler av landet, skriver nyhetsbyrået Reuters.
Det skal være snakk om et amerikansk jagerfly av typen F-35.
Iran sier jagerflyet ble skutt ned i deres luftrom av nytt og avansert luftvernsystem. De sier det er det andre flyet av typen som er skutt ned i løpet av krigen.
Ifølge Iran er det usannsynlig at piloten overlevde, ifølge Reuters.
Verken USAs hovedkommando for Midtøsten (Centcom), Det hvite hus eller forsvarsdepartementet har svart på forespørsler om saken fra nyhetsbyrået AP.
FN utsetter Hormuzmøte – Iran advarer mot provokasjon
FN utsetter et planlagt møte i Sikkerhetsrådet om Hormuzstredet. Foto: Arkivfoto: Seth Wenig / AP / NTBFN utsetter Hormuzmøte – Iran advarer mot provokasjonResolusjonen som FNs sikkerhetsråd skal stemme over kan gi landene i Midtøsten mandat til å beskytte skipstrafikken i Hormuzstredet med makt.
Sikkerhetsrådet skulle etter planen møtes langfredag for å stemme over denne, men møtet er utsatt. Ifølge FN-kilder er det på grunn av påskehøytiden. Det er ikke klart når et nytt møte skal gjennomføres.
– Enhver provoserende handling fra de aggressive og deres støttespillere, inkludert FNs sikkerhetsråd, om situasjonen i Hormuzstredet, vil bare vanskeliggjøre situasjonen, sier Irans utenriksminister Abbas Araghchi fredag.
Kina hadde allerede varslet at de kom til å stemme mot resolusjonen. Som fast medlem i rådet har de vetorett og kan dermed stoppe vedtak.
Trump: Bruer og kraftstasjoner i Iran skal bombes
Foto: Jacquelyn Martin / APTrump: Bruer og kraftstasjoner i Iran skal bombes– Militæret vårt, det største og mektigste i hele verden, har ikke engang begynt å ødelegge noe av det som fortsatt er igjen i Iran. Bruer blir det neste, og deretter kraftstasjoner, skriver Trump i et innlegg på Truth Social.
I innlegget omtaler han nok en gang det han kaller Irans nye regime.
– Det nye regimets lederskap vet hva som må gjøres, og det som må gjøres, må gjøres raskt, skriver han.
Det er uklart hvem Trump snakker om når han snakker om nytt regime i Iran. Irans president er fortsatt den samme som før krigen, Masoud Pezeshkian.
Tidligere torsdag meldte statlig fjernsyn i Iran om angrep på en motorveibru i Karaj, like vest for hovedstaden Teheran. Flere sivile ble drept i angrepene.
Trump skrøt av angrep på bru i Iran – åtte skal være drept og 95 såret
Iran har varslet et knusende svar på Donald trumps trussel om å bombe landet «tilbake til steinalderen» i løpet av de neste to-tre ukene. Foto: Alex Brandon / AP / NTBTrump skrøt av angrep på bru i Iran – åtte skal være drept og 95 såretEi motorveibru som knytter Irans hovedstad Teheran til millionbyen Karaj, ble bombet for andre gang da redningsmannskaper kom til stedet, ifølge iranske medier.
– Den største brua i Iran faller sammen, for aldri igjen å bli brukt. Mye mer kommer! skriver Trump i et innlegg der han har lagt ved et ti sekunder langt videoklipp som skal vise ødeleggelsene.
– Det er på tide at Iran gjør en avtale før det er for sent, og det ikke er noe igjen av det som fortsatt kan bli et storslått land, fortsetter
Trump: Iran må inngå avtale før det er for sent
Foto: Alex Brandon / APTrump: Iran må inngå avtale før det er for sentUSAs president Donald Trump publiserte torsdag en video i sosiale medier av det han sier var Irans største bro.
«Det er på tide for Iran å inngå en avtale før det er for sent», skrev presidenten
En motorveibro som forbinder Irans hovedstad Teheran med byen Kraaj ble truffet torsdag, skriver Reuters, som siterer ifølge Fars news. De skriver videre at ifølge de foreløpige meldingene er flere skadet.
Eide etter Midtøsten-møte med 34 land: – Ber partene søke diplomatiske løsninger
Utenriksminister Espen Barth Eide, her avbildet ved en tidligere anledning. Foto: Terje Pedersen / NTBEide etter Midtøsten-møte med 34 land: – Ber partene søke diplomatiske løsningerNorge og 34 andre land diskuterte umiddelbare tiltak i Hormuzstredet, sier utenriksminister Espen Barth Eide (Ap).
Møtet diskuterte blant annet å sikre transport av særlig viktige råvarer av humanitære grunner, i forståelse med de krigførende parter, opplyser utenriksministeren.
Minst 27 drept og over 100 såret i angrep i Libanon
Redningsmannskaper jobber på stedet etter israelske luftangrep i Beirut onsdag.Minst 27 drept og over 100 såret i angrep i LibanonIsraelske angrep mot Libanon har den siste måneden krevd minst 1345 menneskeliv, blant dem 125 barn, ifølge det libanesiske helsedepartementet.
Det siste døgnet er minst 27 mennesker drept og 105 såret i israelske angrep, opplyser departementet torsdag.
Blant de minst 1345 menneskene som er drept siden 2. mars, er også 91 kvinner. 4040 mennesker er såret.
Blant de drepte er 53 helsearbeidere, opplyser departementet, som har registrert israelske angrep mot hele 82 akuttmedisinske mål.
Hittil er over
Iran: Hevder de har angrepet Amazon i Bahrain
Iran: Hevder de har angrepet Amazon i BahrainDen iranske revolusjonsgarden hevder de har innledet et angrep mot et av Amazons datasentre i Bahrain. Det melder Reuters som siterer statlige iranske medier. Revolusjonsgarden truet tidligere i uken med at den ville angripe amerikanske selskaper i regionen fra 1. april.
Østerrike sier nei til USAs forespørsel om militære overflygninger
Stadig flere europeiske land nekter nå militære amerikanske fly tilgang til sitt luftrom i forbindelse med USAs angrepskrig mot Iran. Foto: AP / NTBØsterrike sier nei til USAs forespørsel om militære overflygningerØsterrike gjør som flere andre europeiske land og har avvist USAs forespørsel om militære overflygninger i forbindelse med angrepskrigen mot Iran.
– Det har vært forespørsler, og de ble avvist fra starten av, sier en talsperson for landets forsvarsdepartement, oberst Michael Bauer.
Han viser til at beslutningen er i tråd med Østerrikes nøytralitetspolitikk, og sier at lignende forespørsler fra andre land som er involvert i krig, også vil bli avvist.
Frankrike og Spania har tidligere kunngjort at de nekter USA å bruke sitt luftrom i forbindelse med krigen mot Iran.
I midten av mars opplyste Sveits at de har gjort det samme.
Ekspert: – Iran har fortsatt betydelig militær kapasitet
Israelske redningsmannskaper på stedet der en iransk rakett slo ned i Tel Aviv 24. mars. Foto: AP / NTBEkspert: – Iran har fortsatt betydelig militær kapasitetIrans militære kapasitet er fortsatt betydelig og sofistikert, sier militæranalytikeren Andreas Krieg ved King's College London.
USAs president Donald Trump hevdet i en TV-tale natt til torsdag at USA har hatt «overveldende seire på slagmarken» i Iran, og at landet ikke lenger utgjør noen stor trussel.
USAs forsvarsminister Pete Hegseth hevdet for få dager siden at Irans militære styrker var nøytralisert.
– Aldri før har et lands militære blitt så raskt og effektivt nøytralisert, sa han.
Militæra
Macron langer ut mot USAs president – sier Trump til stadighet motsier seg selv
Frankrikes president Emmanuel Macron ytrer skarp kritikk av president Donald Trump og sier at angrepskrigen mot Iran ikke vil bringe noen varig løsning på atomspørsmålet. Foto: AP / NTBMacron langer ut mot USAs president – sier Trump til stadighet motsier seg selvPresident Emmanuel Macron anklager Donald Trump for til stadighet å motsi seg selv og for å skape tvil om USAs forpliktelse til Natos kollektive forsvar.
– Dersom man daglig skaper tvil om hvilke forpliktelser man har, så tømmes forpliktelsen for innhold, sier Macron, som torsdag besøkte Sør-Korea.
– Det er for mye snakk som går i alle retninger, la han til.
– Urealistisk
Frankrikes president avviser samtidig kritikken Trump har rettet mot europeiske land som ikke vil bidra militært for å få gjen
Filippinene: Iran lover sikker Hormuz-passasje for olje til Filippinene
Det indiskflaggede skipet Jag Vasant som frakter flytende naturgass, ved havn i Mumbai i India. Skipet er et av få som har fått passere Hormuzstredet de siste ukene. Foto: Rafiq Maqbool / AP / NTBFilippinene: Iran lover sikker Hormuz-passasje for olje til FilippineneIran har lovet å tillate sikker passasje for oljeleveranser til Filippinene gjennom Hormuzstredet, opplyser filippinsk UD.
– Irans utenriksminister forsikret utenriksministeren om at Iran vil tillate sikker, uhindret og rask passasje gjennom Hormuzstredet for filippinske fartøy, energileveranser og alle filippinske sjøfolk, heter det i en uttalelse fra utenriksdepartementet torsdag.
Filippinenes president Ferdinand Marcos erklærte i forrige uke nasjonal energikrise grunnet den globale drivstoffkrisen forårsaket av krigen i Midtøsten.
Bombeberedskap rundt amerikanske banker i Europa – frykter iransk terrorgruppe
Videoer av eksplosjoner er blitt spredt på sosiale medier etter bombeangrep mot jødiske institusjoner. Dette skal være bombeangrepet på en synagoge i Rotterdam 13. mars. Foto: XBombeberedskap rundt amerikanske banker i Europa – frykter iransk terrorgruppeHovedkvarteret til den amerikanske banken Goldman Sachs i Paris ble onsdag kveld er satt under politiovervåking etter trusler fra en iransk gruppe, melder det franske TV-kanalen BFM.
Det skal ha vært amerikanske myndigheter som advarte London-kontoret om at en iransk gruppe truet med å angripe Goldman Sachs-bygninger i Paris med eksplosiver. Derfor har politiet siden onsdag kveld hatt døgnovervåking av hovedkontoret i sentrum av Paris.

sources.news_title: Usa Rescues One of the Pilots of Iran’s Downed Hunt
sources.text:
EEUU rescata a uno de los pilotos del caza derribado por Irán
La búsqueda del segundo tripulante continúa, ya que por el momento su paradero sigue siendo desconocido
Uno de los pilotos del caza estadounidense derribado por Irán este viernes ha sido rescatado por las fuerzas estadounidenses, según han informado dos fuentes oficiales a la cadena CBS News. Mientras, continúa la búsqueda del segundo tripulante, cuyo paradero sigue siendo desconocido y por el que Teherán ha ofrecido una recompensa de 60.000 dólares.
Las imágenes difundidas del lugar del impacto muestran los asientos eyectables separados del fuselaje, lo que sugiere que ambos militares lograron abandonar la aeronave con vida. En la operación de rescate están participando helicópteros Black Hawk, cazas F-35 y drones MQ-9, en un contexto especialmente complejo debido a la llegada de la noche.
Por su parte, los medios iraníes aseguraron inicialmente que los tripulantes habían sido capturados, aunque sin aportar pruebas y con informaciones contradictorias sobre el tipo de aeronave. La Guardia Revolucionaria había ofrecido una recompensa económica muy valiosa por información sobre los pilotos.
Noticia en ampliación

sources.news_title: US fighter jet downed over Iran, rescue mission underway
sources.text:
US Fighter Jet Downed over Iran, Rescue Mision Underway
- The U.S. military is conducting a rescue after a fighter jet was reportedly downed over Iran, escalating regional tensions
- Iran urged its citizens to search for the downed pilot while conducting attacks throughout the Middle East
- A former Iranian diplomat has proposed terms for potential negotiations to end the ongoing conflict
By Jon Gambrell, David Rising and Sam Mednick, Associated Press
DUBAI, United Arab Emirates (AP) — The U.S. military launched a rescue operation Friday after local Iranian state media said an American fighter jet went down over southwest Iran and at least one crew member ejected.
A rescue operation was underway, according to an Israeli military officer briefed on the information who spoke on condition of anonymity ahead of a U.S. announcement.
Social media footage showed American drones, aircraft and helicopters flying over the mountainous region where the Iranian channel said at least one pilot bailed out of the fighter jet.
It would mark the first time the U.S. has lost aircraft in Iranian territory and marks a dramatic escalation in the war since it began five weeks ago. It was not clear if the jet was shot down or crashed. The number of crew on board was not immediately known.
The White House, Pentagon and U.S. Central Command didn't immediately respond to several messages seeking comment.
THIS IS A BREAKING NEWS UPDATE. AP's earlier story follows below.
A channel affiliated with Iranian state television claimed Friday that a U.S. fighter pilot ejected from their aircraft over southwestern Iran. The U.S. did not respond immediately to requests for comment on the claim.
It was not clear what may have happened to the plane, including whether Iran was claiming it was shot down or had another issue. If the claim is confirmed, it could lead to yet another dramatic escalation in the war, nearing the end of its fifth week.
Iran fired on targets across the Mideast on Friday, as Tehran kept the pressure on Israel and its Gulf Arab neighbors, despite U.S. and Israeli insistence that Iran's military capabilities have been all but destroyed.
Iran's attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure and its tight grip on the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of the world's oil and natural gas transits in peacetime, have roiled stock markets, sent oil prices skyrocketing, and threatened to raise the cost of many basic goods, including food.
Television anchor urges residents to hand over pilot
The anchor on the Iranian channel urged residents to hand over any "enemy pilot" to police and promised a reward for anyone who did. The channel is in Kohkilouyeh and Boyer-Ahmad province, an intensely rural and mountainous region that spans over 15,500 square kilometers (5,900 square miles).
Authorities also urged the public to search for the pilot in neighboring Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari province.
Throughout the war, Iran has made a series of claims about shooting down piloted enemy aircraft that turned out not to be true. Friday was the first time that Iran went on television urging the public to look for a suspected downed pilot.
An on-screen crawl earlier urged the public to "shoot them if you see them," referring to social media footage circulating of what appeared to be U.S. aircraft in the area. The channel showed metal debris in the back of a pickup truck while making the announcement but provided no other immediate details.
Iran targets a desalination plant and a refinery
The claim came after Kuwait's Mina al-Ahmadi oil refinery came under Iranian attack, and the state-run Kuwait Petroleum Corp. said firefighters were working to control several blazes.
Kuwait also said an Iranian attack caused "material damage" to a desalination plant. Such plants are responsible for most of the drinking water for Gulf states, and they have become a major target in the war.
Sirens also sounded in Bahrain, Saudi Arabia said it had destroyed several Iranian drones, and Israel reported incoming missiles.
Authorities in the United Arab Emirates shut down a gas field after a missile interception reportedly rained debris on it and started a fire.
Activists reported strikes around Tehran and the central city of Isfahan, but it wasn't immediately clear what was hit. A day earlier, Iran said the U.S. hit a major bridge, which was still under construction, killing eight people.
In Lebanon, where Israel has launched a ground invasion in its fight with the pro-Iranian Hezbollah militant group, an Israeli drone strike on worshippers leaving Friday prayers near Beirut killed two people, according to the state‑run National News Agency
More than 1,900 people have been killed in Iran since the war began on Feb. 28 with U.S. and Israeli strikes. In a review released Friday, the Armed Conflict Location and Event Data, a U.S.-based group, said it found that civilian casualties were clustered around strikes on security and state-linked sites "rather than indiscriminate bombardment" of urban areas.
More than two dozen people have died in Gulf states and the occupied West Bank, 19 have been reported dead in Israel, and 13 U.S. service members have been killed.
More than 1,300 people have been killed and more than 1 million displaced in Lebanon. Ten Israeli soldiers have also died there.
Iran is keeping a chokehold on the Strait of Hormuz
World leaders have struggled to end Iran's stranglehold on the strait, which has had far-reaching consequences for the global economy and has proved to be its greatest strategic advantage in the war.
The U.N. Security Council was expected to take up the matter on Saturday.
U.S. President Donald Trump has vacillated on America's role in the strait, alternately threatening Iran if it doesn't open the waterway and telling other nations to "go get your own oil." On Friday, he said in a post on social media that, "With a little more time, we can easily OPEN THE HORMUZ STRAIT, TAKE THE OIL, & MAKE A FORTUNE."
Spot prices of Brent crude, the international standard, were around $109 Friday, up more than 50% since the start of the war, when Iran began restricting traffic through the strait.
Iran's former top diplomat suggests terms to end the war
Former Iranian Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif — a diplomat with long experience negotiating with the West who remains close to a pragmatic wing of Iran's leadership — wrote on Friday in Foreign Affairs magazine that the time has come to end what he referred to as a stalemate.
The U.S. and Iran have proposed dueling plans, and Zarif's proposal included elements of both in a sign part of Iran's leadership might be willing to negotiate.
Iran "should offer to place limits on its nuclear program and to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for an end to all sanctions — a deal Washington wouldn't take before but might accept now," he wrote.
It's not clear how much to read into the proposal from Zarif, who has no official position in Iran's government, but would likely not have published such a piece without at least some authorization from senior leaders.
Rising reported from Bangkok. Associated Press writers Sylvie Corbet in Paris, Sarah El Deeb in Beirut, Tong-hyung Kim in Seoul, South Korea, and Michelle L. Price in Washington contributed to this report.
